title: KV Cache Allocator & Fragmentation Metrics (Runtime Architecture)
author: Noah Patel
content:
h1. KV Cache Allocator & Fragmentation Metrics (Runtime Architecture)

This page documents the serving runtime’s KV cache allocator internals, fragmentation definitions, and the telemetry we rely on to detect fragmentation-induced tail latency and OOM risk.

Scope:
* GPU KV cache allocation for decode (and prefill where applicable)
* Block map metadata and compaction/eviction-related accounting
* Observability: counters, gauges, histograms, and structured logs
* Component interaction contracts (Scheduler, Prefix Cache, Kernels)

Non-scope:
* Attention kernel math or model semantics
* Host memory staging caches
* Control-plane UX (see dashboard spec for visualization)

---

h2. Background & why fragmentation matters

The runtime uses a GPU-resident KV cache to avoid recomputing attention history during decoding. Under bursty traffic and mixed sequence lengths, the KV cache develops “holes” as sequences complete or are evicted, and as blocks are acquired/released unevenly across streams.

Consequences observed in production:
* Increased allocator overhead (search / bookkeeping) on the hot path
* Higher frequency of expensive reallocations when contiguous space is scarce
* Increased OOM risk due to inability to satisfy allocations despite sufficient total free bytes
* Bursty p95/p99 spikes correlated with allocation failures and eviction/compaction churn

---

h2. Terminology

* *KV cache*: GPU memory storing per-layer keys/values for active sequences.
* *Block*: the smallest allocation unit the allocator manages (fixed size per device/pool). Each block holds KV for a fixed number of tokens (token capacity depends on model dims + quantization profile).
* *Span*: a contiguous run of blocks assigned to a single sequence (or a single logical “sequence segment”).
* *Hole*: free blocks located between allocated spans.
* *External fragmentation*: free capacity exists, but split into holes such that a request cannot allocate the needed span(s) under current constraints.
* *Internal fragmentation*: allocated space not fully utilized due to rounding to block size or early EOS.
* *Movable block*: a block that may be migrated by the compaction engine, subject to kernel synchronization constraints.

---

h2. High-level architecture

At runtime, KV cache memory management is split into:

1) *Fast-path allocator* (per device/pool)
* Issues/reclaims KV blocks on every decode step.
* Must be bounded and predictable (avoid unbounded scans).

2) *Eviction policy* (scheduler-aware)
* Chooses victims when pressure is high or admission requires reclaim.
* Integrates with tenant tiering / fairness.

3) *Compaction engine* (optional, feature-flagged)
* Re-packs blocks to reduce holes and improve future allocation success.
* Operates under a budget to protect median latency.

4) *Observability layer*
* Metrics and logs for fragmentation state, eviction churn, and compaction cost.

Text diagram (control/data flow):

Scheduler
  | (admission, priority classes, cache-pressure signals)
  v
Runtime request execution (prefill/decode)
  | (needs KV blocks; can hit pressure)
  v
KV allocator (block map)
  |--> success: returns block handles for kernel
  |--> fail: emit alloc_failure + request eviction/compaction hints
             |
             v
        Eviction policy  -----> Prefix cache interaction (reuse vs drop)
             |
             v
        Free blocks returned to allocator

Compaction engine (when enabled)
  | (moves blocks + updates metadata under sync constraints)
  v
Allocator state becomes less fragmented

---

h2. Allocator internals

h3. Allocation model

The allocator manages a fixed-size KV arena per GPU (or per logical GPU slice) and exposes:
* allocate(sequence_id, blocks_needed, priority_class) -> block_span_handle
* free(sequence_id) -> returns blocks to free lists
* grow(sequence_id, additional_blocks) -> extends span where possible or allocates a new span (implementation depends on move semantics and kernel addressing mode)

Design goals:
* O(1) or bounded-time allocations in the steady state
* Avoid global locks on the critical path (per-device lock sharding; lock-free reads where possible)
* Stable accounting for “used/free/fragmented” for observability and trigger policies

h3. Block map and metadata

Each device/pool maintains:
* *Block table* (size = total_blocks)
  * state: FREE | ALLOCATED | RESERVED_FOR_MOVE
  * owner: sequence_id (or 0 for FREE)
  * generation: monotonic counter to prevent stale handles
  * next/prev pointers for free-list and span-list membership

* *Free lists* (segregated by span length)
  * We track free spans by run length to reduce scans.
  * For simplicity, lengths are bucketed (e.g., 1,2,4,8,… up to max).

* *Sequence span list*
  * sequences may own multiple spans (e.g., when growth cannot be contiguous).
  * spans carry token range metadata to map token index -> (span, offset).

* *Accounting*
  * total_blocks
  * used_blocks
  * free_blocks
  * reserved_blocks (for in-flight moves / staging)

Notes:
* The allocator is block-based to make fragmentation observable and compaction feasible.
* See ADR-0127 for the block size decision and move semantics.

h3. Threading and synchronization model (summary)

Constraints:
* Kernels may read KV addresses while decode is in flight.
* Compaction can only move blocks when we can guarantee no in-flight kernel will dereference old addresses.

Rules of thumb:
* *Fast path (allocate/free)*: guarded by per-device mutex (or shard locks), but must not wait on GPU.
* *Moves (compaction)*: require explicit stream/event synchronization gates.
  * Move planning can run on CPU without GPU sync.
  * Move execution must publish an “address update barrier” before any kernel can see new handles.

Implementation detail:
* We rely on a “KV address epoch” mechanism: kernels read an epoch and only consume block addresses consistent with that epoch. Compaction increments epoch after completing moves and publishing updated metadata.

---

h2. Fragmentation definitions (what we measure)

Fragmentation is not a single number; we track multiple signals to answer different operational questions.

h3. 1) External fragmentation ratio

Definition:
*external_fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_free_span_blocks / free_blocks)*

Interpretation:
* 0.0 is ideal (all free blocks are contiguous in one span).
* Near 1.0 indicates free blocks are heavily split into holes.

Operational use:
* High external fragmentation increases allocation failure probability for large-span requests (e.g., long-context decode growth).

h3. 2) Allocation failure rate

Definition:
*alloc_failure = allocator could not satisfy blocks_needed without eviction/compaction*

We track:
* Count of failures
* Count of failures “recovered” via eviction within the same scheduling tick
* Count of failures that bubble up to admission control / request rejection

h3. 3) Internal fragmentation estimate

We estimate internal fragmentation at the sequence level:
*internal_frag_bytes = (allocated_token_capacity - actual_tokens_stored) * bytes_per_token*

This is an estimate because “actual_tokens_stored” may be approximate for streaming decode.

Operational use:
* Helps tune block size and growth strategy; not used for paging alerts.

h3. 4) Effective KV capacity utilization

Definition:
*effective_utilization = used_blocks / total_blocks*

We also track “available-for-allocation”:
*(free_blocks - reserved_blocks) / total_blocks*

Operational use:
* Capacity planning and admission control.

h3. 5) Hole distribution

We track a histogram of free span lengths (in blocks). This is used to distinguish:
* many tiny holes (allocator churn) vs
* a small number of medium holes (better candidate for compaction)

---

h2. Metrics & telemetry

All metrics are emitted by the runtime per device pool (and aggregated at pool/region). The canonical names below match the telemetry schema used by Observability Pack.

h3. Metric conventions

* Prefix: runtime_kv_cache_* for KV cache allocator/compaction/eviction
* Units:
  * blocks for block counts
  * bytes for memory sizes
  * seconds for wall time
  * microseconds for fast-path allocator time
* Required labels:
  * region
  * pool (hosted pool or dedicated pool name)
  * model_family (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen; exact values from model registry)
  * gpu_type (e.g., h100, a100; if available)
  * runtime_build (short hash or build id)

h3. Allocator state (gauges)

* runtime_kv_cache_total_blocks{region,pool,gpu_type} (gauge)
* runtime_kv_cache_used_blocks{region,pool,model_family} (gauge)
* runtime_kv_cache_free_blocks{region,pool,model_family} (gauge)
* runtime_kv_cache_reserved_blocks{region,pool,model_family} (gauge)

h3. Fragmentation metrics (gauges + histograms)

* runtime_kv_cache_largest_free_span_blocks{region,pool,model_family} (gauge)
* runtime_kv_cache_external_fragmentation_ratio{region,pool,model_family} (gauge, 0..1)
* runtime_kv_cache_free_span_blocks_bucket{region,pool,model_family,le} (histogram)
  * Bucket boundaries are in blocks (1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,+Inf)

h3. Allocation outcomes (counters)

* runtime_kv_cache_alloc_requests_total{region,pool,model_family} (counter)
* runtime_kv_cache_alloc_success_total{region,pool,model_family} (counter)
* runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failure_total{region,pool,model_family,reason} (counter)
  * reason ∈ {insufficient_free, fragmented_free, reserved_pressure, invariant_violation}

h3. Allocator latency (histogram)

* runtime_kv_cache_alloc_duration_us_bucket{region,pool,model_family,le} (histogram)
* runtime_kv_cache_free_duration_us_bucket{region,pool,model_family,le} (histogram)

Guidance:
* This is CPU wall time for allocator operations. It is a strong leading indicator of hot-path regression.

h3. Eviction metrics (counters)

* runtime_kv_cache_evictions_total{region,pool,model_family,priority_class,eviction_reason} (counter)
  * eviction_reason ∈ {admission_pressure, allocation_failure, compaction_planning, ttl_expired}

* runtime_kv_cache_evicted_blocks_total{region,pool,model_family} (counter)

h3. Compaction metrics (when enabled)

* runtime_kv_cache_compaction_runs_total{region,pool,model_family,trigger} (counter)
  * trigger ∈ {frag_threshold, alloc_failure, interval_maintenance, manual}

* runtime_kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total{region,pool,model_family} (counter)

* runtime_kv_cache_compaction_duration_ms_bucket{region,pool,model_family,le} (histogram)

* runtime_kv_cache_compaction_budget_exhausted_total{region,pool,model_family} (counter)

* runtime_kv_cache_compaction_aborted_total{region,pool,model_family,reason} (counter)
  * reason ∈ {inflight_kernels, sync_timeout, allocator_lock_contention, safety_guardrail}

h3. Structured logs (sampling)

We emit structured log events for correlation with tail latency and request traces.

Event: kv_alloc_failure
* fields: request_id, sequence_id, blocks_needed, free_blocks, largest_free_span, fragmentation_ratio, priority_class, tenant_tier, region, pool, model, build

Event: kv_compaction_summary
* fields: run_id, trigger, bytes_moved, blocks_moved, duration_ms, pre_frag_ratio, post_frag_ratio, aborted (bool), abort_reason

Sampling policy:
* allocation failure events: log 100% (they should be rare)
* compaction summary: log 1/N (configurable) + always log when aborted

---

h2. Component interactions & contracts

h3. Scheduler <-> KV cache contract

The scheduler is the “traffic shaping” layer and should not assume the allocator is a simple free-bytes pool. Contract:

Scheduler provides to allocator:
* priority_class (derived from tenant tier / SLA class)
* request deadlines / latency class (used only for eviction/compaction urgency decisions)

Allocator provides to scheduler:
* cache_pressure_level (enum): OK | ELEVATED | CRITICAL
  * OK: fragmentation_ratio below threshold and alloc_failure_rate low
  * ELEVATED: fragmentation rising; allocator latency increasing
  * CRITICAL: alloc failures or largest_free_span too small for typical growth

Scheduler actions by pressure level (guidance):
* OK: normal admission
* ELEVATED: mild backpressure on long-context requests; prefer batching and stable tenants
* CRITICAL: enforce admission control (cap concurrent long-context), prefer short decodes, consider routing to other pool/region; if compaction enabled, allow one maintenance slice per interval

See ADR-0129 for eviction policy and fairness constraints.

h3. Prefix cache interaction

Prefix cache increases reuse by keeping KV for common prefixes, but can worsen fragmentation if not coordinated.

Guidelines:
* Prefix cache entries are eligible for eviction under CRITICAL pressure unless tenant is pinned / premium.
* Prefix cache should expose “reuse likelihood” metadata (hit rate / last access) to eviction policy.
* When compaction is enabled, compaction planning must treat pinned prefix segments as immovable (or move with explicit safety barriers and separate budget).

Observability linkage:
* Spikes in evictions_total with eviction_reason=compaction_planning often indicate we are “paying eviction” instead of moving, which can harm quality for prefix-heavy workloads.

h3. Kernels / addressability constraints

Kernels consume block addresses for KV reads/writes.

Key constraints:
* If blocks are movable, kernels must tolerate address changes across steps.
* Address changes may only occur at safe points (epoch barriers) to avoid reading stale addresses.

Operational warning:
* If you see compaction_aborted_total{reason=inflight_kernels} rising, it typically means our planned safe points are not being reached due to long-running kernels or stream scheduling issues. This is often correlated with p99 regressions.

---

h2. Interpreting the metrics (common patterns)

h3. Pattern A: High fragmentation ratio + low free blocks

Symptoms:
* external_fragmentation_ratio > 0.75
* free_blocks low (< 10%)
* alloc_failures increasing

Likely cause:
* True capacity pressure (too many active sequences) + fragmentation.

Actions:
* Reduce concurrency / enable admission controls for long-context traffic
* Verify eviction is functioning (evictions_total increases)
* If compaction is enabled: ensure budget not exhausted and moves are not aborting

h3. Pattern B: High fragmentation ratio + plenty of free blocks

Symptoms:
* free_blocks moderate (> 20%)
* largest_free_span small
* alloc_failures for large allocations

Likely cause:
* External fragmentation due to mixed-length churn.

Actions:
* Consider enabling compaction in canary pool
* If compaction already enabled: tune triggers/budget (see ADR-0128) and confirm compaction reduces post_frag_ratio

h3. Pattern C: Allocator duration increases without fragmentation increase

Symptoms:
* alloc_duration_us p95/p99 increases
* fragmentation_ratio stable

Likely cause:
* Lock contention, pathological free-list scanning, or instrumentation overhead.

Actions:
* Capture CPU profiles; check allocator lock hold time
* Validate metric cardinality (model labels) is bounded

---

h2. Dashboards & alerts (what oncall should watch)

The KV Cache Health dashboard provides pool/region drill-down.

Recommended alert signals (initial guidance; see SRE SLO page for final thresholds):
* Allocation failures:
  * runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failure_total rate > 1/min for 10m (page, hosted)
  * any sustained failures in dedicated pools (ticket + oncall review)

* Fragmentation:
  * external_fragmentation_ratio > 0.8 for 15m AND largest_free_span_blocks < P50(blocks_needed_for_growth) (warn)

* Compaction regressions (when enabled):
  * compaction_duration_ms p99 > budget target for 15m (warn)
  * compaction_aborted_total rate > 5/min (warn; investigate safe points)

---

h2. Runtime flags (relevant to allocator + observability)

Names are representative; refer to in-code config docs for the exact runtime flag keys.

* kv_cache.enable_compaction (default: false)
* kv_cache.compaction.trigger_frag_ratio (default: 0.75)
* kv_cache.compaction.interval_seconds (default: 30)
* kv_cache.compaction.budget_ms_per_interval (default: 2)
* kv_cache.eviction.mode (default: scheduler_aware_v1)
* kv_cache.metrics.enable_free_span_histogram (default: true)

Rollout note:
* All compaction functionality must remain behind a flag with safe rollback (disable compaction; keep metrics).

---

Owners:

Any changes to:
* metric names/labels
* fragmentation definitions
* allocator invariants

…must include:
* a small perf-canary run covering bursty mixed-length traffic
* updated dashboard spec if panels/queries change
* a migration plan for renamed metrics (do not break existing alert rules)

---

h2. Appendix: Quick reference table

| Concept | Signal | Primary consumer |
|---|---|---|
| External fragmentation | runtime_kv_cache_external_fragmentation_ratio | SRE + runtime oncall |
| Contiguity | runtime_kv_cache_largest_free_span_blocks | allocator/compaction planning |
